new.headline: A clean, quiet first week back earns a small step up: same three run days, with each running interval growing from 1.5 min to 2 min. Keep every effort easy and stop at the first sign of shin ache.

new.analysis:
The plan nudges one thing at a time, because that is how return weeks are supposed to feel almost boring. Your shin stayed at 0/10 across three sessions and was quiet the next morning, and your heart rate sat comfortably in zones 1 and 2. That earns a small step, not a big one.

The step this week is the length of each running interval, from 1.5 min to 2 min, while the walk stays at 1 min. Total running minutes move from about 22 to about 32, which is more than 10 percent, so the trade is holding the number of sessions at three and keeping the walk recoveries long. If anything feels off on Monday, drop back to 1.5 min running and tell me.

Your pain-free streak is 1 of 4 weeks. Four clean weeks in a row is when we start thinking about strides, hills or faster running. Until then, every run stays easy, on flat ground, with the walk breaks honoured even if you feel great. Keep the physio calf and hip work twice this week, since it is almost certainly part of why the shin has been quiet.

One note on Saturday: heart rate drifted up a few beats by the end, which can just be heat or a slightly quicker last interval. Keep Saturday to the same cadence as Mon and Wed and let effort, not pace, lead.

settingsProposalBullets: Target of 30 min continuous running by mid-October is noted as your goal; I will plan backwards from it each week.
Preferred run days are Mon, Wed and Sat per your physio; I will keep that pattern unless you tell me otherwise.

safetyCallouts.title: Stop and call the physio if the shin aches.
safetyCallouts.body: Any pain during a run above 3/10, pain that is worse the next morning, or a return of the original shin symptom means pause running and check in with your physio before the next session.
